channel.title: Cognation
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Cognation" - Blood from an empty universe used as a reality-sink holds a dark idea

item.title: Re: Cognation
item.content:encoded:
This isn't a cliché idea, really; there's just too much going on. You have multiple ideas (The Foundation finds blood and starts using it! The blood flows towards people thinking of certain things! Scranton Reality Anchors! 3001! Ichabod project! Dr. Scranton! Old gods! 231!), but they don't fit together thematically or mechanically. Trying to put all of them together leads to a complex mess that's less than the sum of its parts.

If one of the ideas presented here was excised and fleshed out it might make for a compelling article (the Foundation stumbling on anomalous blood and trying to meddle with it is probably the most compelling, though it would take some work to make it interesting), but as-is I'm not particularly enthused.

Good luck!

item.title: Re: Cognation
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there DeLuChanel . Let’s take a look at your concept.

So I initially commented that the concept wasn’t clear from your summary. I know you’re constrained by the word count, so I’m giving you the benefit of the doubt and asking for further elaboration on the concept.

I still don’t understand what the main anomaly is. Basically, is it the blood in your elevator pitch? Is it the broken wormhole? You’ve branched off into scp instances quite rapidly without explaining what the base concept is supposed to be.

Regarding your central narrative, I understand the first portion, but you spend a good deal of it explaining how SRAs work and how your SCP affects them. This is cool and all, but what’s the impact on the actual narrative.

Then, you go into another type of blood for some reason, and we get another SCP instance. It’s all VERY convoluted.

Typically, we would advise new writers to start with a simple concept and minimise the number and types of instances. Also, there seems to be frequent cross-links with other SCPs which I’m not entirely sure why besides passing references.

Okay, tl;dr, do try and elaborate on the following questions in another post below:

1) What is the base anomaly? What is special about it?
2) How does the Foundation plan to contain it (briefly)
3) What is the significance of the anomaly to the wider universe? What are the implications / themes you wish to hit?

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop another PM and I'll do my best to reply below. All the best!

item.title: Re: Cognation : AKA The Ballad of King Robert
Cognation
item.content:encoded:
Blood from an empty universe that is used as a reality sink within mass produced SRAs holds secrets of beginning and endings.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mystery/Horror

Page Layout: Standard layout, addendum

Elevator Pitch: The abuse and overuse of an anomalous type of blood in SRAs slowly leads to its corruption. Meanwhile questions about its source leads an obsessed researcher to a dark theory.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: While experimenting with broken-wormhole creation the Foundation access an 'empty-universe' classed as SCP-6334-A; a temporally non-linear, spatially-infinitely dimension with a minute hume level. Through access, they encounters an anomalous blood (SCP-6334-1).Through testing the foundation discovers when a small charge is conducted through SCP-6334-1 it creates a powerful reality-sink (when humes are drawn from the immediate environment into a dimension with a low concentration of reality). In this case SCP-6334-A. Testing also proves the substance can be collected from 6334-A indefinitely.

Availability and strength of reality-sinks lead the Foundation to use them in a type of Scranton Reality Anchors; this utilizes both a reality-sink and a reality-source. These reality-sources are purportedly lobotomized reality benders from the Ichabod Campaign from SCP-4231. In 2001, Dr. Robert Scranton is involved 6334-1 collection which goes wrong, is drawn into SCP-3001 and another type of blood is discovered. Classified as SCP-6334-2; it is in a constant reality-sink. This requires SRAs to be properly contained. Experiments show that 6334-2 also senses thoughts around certain concepts (specifically marriage, the colour red and hemophobia). It will attempt to flow towards the thoughts' source(s) and attempt entry into the human body.

6334-1 amounts start to convert into 6334-2 at an ever-increasing rate. A researcher for 6334 receives a transcript of "Dust and Blood" and a 6334-2 vial from a colleague assigned to SCP-231. This leads him to send a drone into SCP-6334-A, discovering an corpse-like entity. An interview is conducted wherein the researcher claims a number of things; that the entity is Dr. Robert Scranton and SCP-6334-A is actually SCP-3001, that the foundation has a weak god in the darkness of the abyss/continued use of 6334-1 is feeding other 'gods' to it and that the 6334 vial is from 231-7 and she is his blood after all. He then asked "What really happened to Anna, his first bride?".

Hook/Attention Grabber: Similar ideas have been explored before like "Until Death" but frankly there is way more evidence/similarities between SK and Dr. Scranton.

Additional Notes: I know this is a cliché/eye-rolling idea, but the fact this idea hasn't been explored is shocking (given the evidence). Willing to delve into more detail about the parallels between Scranton and the Scarlet King, Please inquire if curious/need convincing.
